tasks.title: One tree resolver for every hook, attribution from the rows, and git read only in command position
tasks.description: Field report on 3.0.1, reproduced at HEAD: only require-plan re-roots onto a linked worktree (_config.path_tree). guard-secrets-read judges shell writes against CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR's plan ('Phase P41 is in_progress' for an executor in the P48 worktree) and skips out-of-root worktree targets; guard-capabilities applies main's area policy; remind-tdd is silent; guard-history-rewrite, journal-writes, guard-edits, meter-usage and detect-plan-skip use repo_root. One _config.tree_for(data, target) over path_tree/command_tree, every manifest/state reader calls it, and a lint over hooks/ (hosted where the cross-file lints live, reading source only - hooks may not import scripts) bans a bare repo_root beside a manifest or state read. journal-writes then derives task.complete/task.commit for a worktree's writes. guard-bash-writes blames a shell command for journal rows the plugin's own writers appended (peer session hook rows, CLI rows filed under another --project state dir, a merge): bind the verdict to content - new rows that chain validly onto the committed tail with via hook/cli/panel and a fresh ts are named as the plugin's writer; bytes equal to a version reachable from MERGE_HEAD/ORIG_HEAD are 'brought in by the merge'; otherwise the tamper notice stands; peer sidecar claims stay unread. guard-history-rewrite denies 'echo ... git stash' and a piped heredoc body 'cat <<EOF | python3 x.py -' containing the words: recognise git only in command position (start, ; && || | newline, or after xargs/sudo/env/bash -c), classify a piped heredoc body by the far side of the pipe; 'true && git stash push' stays DENY.

tasks.title: Sign-off review findings: the history guard reads line continuations, piped heredocs and substitutions the way bash does, ORIG_HEAD acquits only inside the window, and the tree lint binds to what the code does
tasks.description:
Findings of the phase review, every one to be fixed (or answered with a measured reason) in this task:
R1 (high) plugins/audit/hooks/guard-history-rewrite.py:286-313 (_inert_span / _inert_opening, fed by _shell_pieces:241-262): A line continuation gets past the inert-emitter exemption. shlex keeps an escaped newline as its own piece, and _SEP_ONLY classes that piece as a separator. So the emitter's span ends there, and the pipe on the continued line is read as a new command. In bash, backslash-newline is removed, so the emitter's output really is piped into the shell. I called the functions directly with bytecode writes off, on the base and on HEAD. These were REFUSED on the base and are ALLOWED on HEAD: `echo git push --force origin main` + backslash-newline + `  | sh` (always_refused: base WHY_FORCE, HEAD None); `echo git rebase -i HEAD~2` + backslash-newline + ` | sh` (base WHY_REBASE, HEAD None); `echo git stash` + backslash-newline + tab + `| bash` (moving_stash: base [''], HEAD []). Only the spelling with no whitespace after the newline is still caught, because there the `|` shares a piece with the newline. I confirmed bash joins the lines by running `echo hi` + backslash-newline + `  | tr h H` through bash, which printed `Hi`. No gp* case covers a continuation. -> In _shell_pieces, remove backslash-newline outside quotes before lexing, as bash does. Add deny cases next to gp8/gp18 for the stash, force-push and rebase spellings above.
R2 (high) plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py:1368-1414 (_pipe_reads_data), used by split_heredocs:1492 and so by both guard-history-rewrite and guard-secrets-read: The detail of this finding was withheld by a safety classifier when the report was first delivered, and it is deliberately not written out again here. What can be said: I have a base-vs-HEAD comparison showing that the new far-side-of-the-pipe classification drops, as data, a heredoc body that the base graded as a program. Because split_heredocs is shared, this reaches guard-secrets-read as well as the history guard. -> Have a maintainer review which operands _pipe_reads_data (and the head-form _STDIN_INTERP beside it) accepts as a SCRIPT operand, against every spelling an interpreter accepts for reading its program from stdin. Keep one shared set that answers 'program, keep graded'. Add red-first deny cases in test_guard_secrets_read.py and in the gq* table.
R3 (med) plugins/audit/hooks/guard-bash-writes.py:1379 (_ORIGIN_REFS), 1484-1487 (journal_origin); SECURITY.md:608-625: The ORIG_HEAD acquittal is not tied to this window. ORIG_HEAD persists from any earlier reset, rebase or merge. So a shell command that restores a journal file to that version is reported as 'brought in by the merge' - for example `git show ORIG_HEAD:<journal> > <journal>`, or `git checkout ORIG_HEAD -- docs/audit/journal/`. Such a restore can drop committed rows while the chain that remains still verifies. No case exercises ORIG_HEAD at all: ja7/ja8 drive MERGE_HEAD only. So removing ORIG_HEAD from _ORIGIN_REFS, or accepting a stale one, would both survive the suite. -> Accept ORIG_HEAD only when HEAD moved inside this pass's window, e.g. the ORIG_HEAD ref file's mtime >= since, or a HEAD sha recorded at the previous look that differs now. Never acquit a file whose bytes are a truncation of HEAD's blob. Add a stale-ORIG_HEAD case that must keep the tamper notice, and a fresh `git reset HEAD~1` case that is acquitted.
R4 (low) SECURITY.md:187-197; CHANGELOG.md:170-176: Both documents say `git` counts only in command position (the start of a command, after a separator, or as the argument of a runner). The code does not do that. git_calls still counts every `git` word except those in an inert emitter's span. Measured on HEAD: `grep -n git stash notes.md`, `ls git stash` and `cat git stash` all give moving_stash == [''], i.e. they are refused as a stash. This errs toward over-refusal, but it is a changed SECURITY.md sentence that is not true of the code. It also means the phase's desiredOutcome clause is not met as written (see intent). -> Either reword both documents to say what the code does - every `git` word counts except the arguments of a closed list of inert emitters whose output reaches no shell - or implement real command-position reading, with allow cases for grep/ls/cat.
R5 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/_deps.py:1500-1573 (hook_tree_violations): The lint binds to the spelling `_config.repo_root`, not to what the code does. The migrated shape `_config.tree_for(data, _config.PROJECT_ONLY)['project']` handed to a HOOK_TREE_READER is the identical defect, and it passes. guard-bash-writes.decide does exactly this, on purpose. An alias (`rr = _config.repo_root; rr(data)`) also evades it, because _config_call_name needs the attribute spelled at the call. The docstring admits the PROJECT_ONLY route. The SECURITY.md/CHANGELOG wording is literally accurate, but the desiredOutcome's 'keeps a bare repo_root from coming back' is all the lint guarantees. -> Also flag a scope chain that calls a HOOK_TREE_READER where every tree_for call it can reach passes PROJECT_ONLY, unless the file is in a declared exemption table with a checked reason (guard-bash-writes: one watched tree). Treat a Name bound from `_config.repo_root` as the call itself.
R6 (low) plugins/audit/hooks/guard-history-rewrite.py:855-861, 908-911 (command_roots / git_root choice): When a command reaches several trees, the ancestry question is asked only in roots[1]. Refs resolve per worktree (HEAD, HEAD~n, ORIG_HEAD), so in `git -C <wtA> status; git -C <wtB> reset --hard HEAD~1` the reset's HEAD~1 is resolved in wtA. The comment ('the first worktree it reaches') states the behaviour but not that it can be the wrong tree. -> Pair each invocation with its own directory (git_calls already returns it) and ask orphaned_by per invocation, in that invocation's tree.
R7 (low) plugins/audit/hooks/guard-history-rewrite.py:169-177 (INERT_PROGRAMS comment); SECURITY.md:187-197: The emitter exemption widens the write-then-execute gap to unquoted `echo`. `echo git stash > x.sh; sh x.sh` and `echo git stash >> ~/.bashrc` were refused on the base and are allowed on HEAD. The module header records this class for heredoc and printf spellings. But the INERT_PROGRAMS comment says 'the cost of an omission is a refusal', and the new SECURITY.md paragraph does not say that emitting into a file that is later executed is now read as prose. -> State it next to the inert list in SECURITY.md and in the INERT_PROGRAMS comment, or keep an emitter graded when its redirect target is a shell script or shell rc file. Either way, add a case that records the choice.
pre-existing 101 (med) plugins/audit/hooks/guard-history-rewrite.py:_SEP_SPLIT / _shell_pieces: A double-quoted command substitution is never read as an operation. `echo "$(git stash)"`, `eval "$(echo git stash)"` and `sh -c "$(echo git stash)"` lex to one word, 'git stash', which is not the word `git`. Allowed on the base and on HEAD alike. -> Re-parse the contents of `$(...)` and backquotes found inside a double-quoted word as a nested command, through the same git_calls door.
pre-existing 102 (low) plugins/audit/hooks/guard-history-rewrite.py:git_calls: When `xargs git` takes the verb from stdin, the operation is not seen: `echo stash | xargs git`, and a heredoc piped to `xargs git`, are allowed on the base and on HEAD. The SECURITY.md sentence naming xargs as a runner holds only when the verb is on the command line. -> Treat `xargs git` (git as the runner's program, with no verb after it) as an unknown verb that is refused while a plan exists, or state the residual.

outcome.technical: join_continuations before lexing; piped heredoc data only for cat+quoted into a plain script file; nested quoted substitutions; window-bound MERGE_HEAD/ORIG_HEAD; behaviour-bound tree lint with a declared exemption.

tasks.title: journal-writes derives no sign-off from a stored status, and no row for a write another session made
tasks.description: Measured on this repo: after the orchestrator's settle (which stored the derived done on 34 phase bodies and mirrored status onto 69 index stubs), a DIFFERENT session's installed journal-writes hook, on an unrelated Bash call, derived 147 rows under its own session - 105 phase.signoff for 70 phases - from the manifest digest change it saw. Two defects compose. (1) Meaning: a sign-off is recorded by the signoff verb (its own journal row); a stored-status flip is not a sign-off - at HEAD phase.signoff is derived only from phase bodies, but a parent-branch body settle moved to done has mergedAt null, and a null last field is never a dedup key, so HEAD still derives one per such body. Stop deriving phase.signoff from status (or derive it only from a review.status/verdict change the verb did not record), and recognise settle and the stub mirror as the plugin's own materialisation (settle journals plan.settle). (2) Attribution: the sweep lane derives rows from any manifest digest change it sees, whoever wrote it, and files them under the observing session. Derive only from writes this tool call made - its own target, or the command's tree through tree_for - never from a digest a peer's write moved. Cases: settle, then a peer session's unrelated Bash call derives nothing; a hand status flip still yields a hand-edit row; the verb's sign-off row is not duplicated.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_journal_writes.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a status flip to done written by settle is derived as a phase.signoff row by the next hook sweep, under the observing session

outcome.technical: Pre pass refreshes moved slots; phase.signoff derived from its inputs, not the stored status.
outcome.descriptive: A session's hook no longer records another session's plan writes as its own, and storing a status is never read as a sign-off.

tasks.title: A session's journal writer is keyed by its worktree too, so parallel worktrees of one session never share a file
tasks.description: Hit merging main into P70: audit-journal merge refused 2026-09.<session>.jsonl because rows written in two linked worktrees of ONE session at the same second said different things (task starts in sibling worktrees), and timestamp order cannot separate them; it was resolved by hand. The per-writer file layout that makes journal merges conflict-free assumes one writer per file, but the writer id is the session id, so every worktree a session drives appends the same basename. Key the writer by session AND worktree (a linked worktree's .claude/state already holds its own writer token) so two worktrees never share a file; keep reading existing session-keyed files; check verify, merge, doctor and the record-key dedup read the new names. Cases: two worktrees of one session write two files; the old name is still read; a merge of both branches has no journal conflict.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__journal_io.py: repro that FAILS on current code - two linked worktrees driven by one session resolve the same journal writer file

outcome.technical: _journal_io.worktree_key keys file_for for the journal and the evidence ledger in a linked worktree; main keeps the session name; readers list the directory.
outcome.descriptive: Parallel worktrees driven by one session write their own journal and evidence files, so merging them never conflicts.

tasks.title: Second-review findings: the history guard keeps only narrowings it can prove, journal-writes records what nobody explained, and the worktree key is asked of git
tasks.description:
Second review of P72's fixes. Decision recorded by the orchestrator: the history guard is FAIL-LOUD, and two of its narrowings cannot be proven - each fix of them opened a new pass (a comment ending in a backslash, a later pipe stage, an interpreter option in the environment, an emitter writing a file run by name or by git itself). So REMOVE the inert-emitter exemption and the piped-heredoc-as-data classification, returning both to the base's grading; the need the field report named is already met by feeding the heredoc to the script directly (python3 x.py --technical - <<'EOF'), which the base allows. Keep every tightening: continuation join (made comment-aware - an unquoted # at a word start runs to end of line, no join inside it), quoted substitutions read as commands (and an unparseable inner body REFUSES instead of contributing nothing, quotes tracked inside $( )), xargs git from stdin, per-invocation trees, window-bound merge acquittal, the behaviour-bound lint. Then fix the rest of the review: journal-writes must not silently absorb a between-calls move no trail row explains (record it as observed between calls, unattributed), phase.signoff derived from the inputs on BOTH sides, the worktree key decided by git (git-dir vs git-common-dir, token in the worktree's own git dir) with COMPATIBILITY.md naming whatever limit remains, ImportFrom aliases and stale exemption rows in the lint, every reset --hard target graded, and a here-string word fed to a shell or interpreter graded as a command. SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG say exactly what the code does, including the over-refusal that remains on purpose.
Findings:
R1 (high) plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py:1485-1517 (join_continuations), used by guard-history-rewrite.py:260 (_shell_pieces) and :508 (_quoted_substitutions): NEW ALLOW, introduced by the R1 fix. join_continuations removes backslash-newline everywhere outside single quotes, including inside a shell comment. In bash a comment runs to the end of the line, so a backslash at the end of a comment does NOT continue the line: `bash -c 'echo hi # \<newline>echo SECOND-LINE-RAN'` printed both lines. After the join, the next line's words become arguments of the inert emitter (`#` is an ordinary word because commenters is empty), so the git command on the next line is skipped. I loaded each tree's hooks with bytecode writes off, from git-archive exports of 036e98e, c9a2333 and HEAD. `echo hi # \<nl>git stash`: moving_stash is [''] on base and c9, [] on HEAD. `: # \<nl>git stash`: the same. `true # \<nl>git push --force origin main`: always_refused is truthy on base and c9, None on HEAD. So a force-push and a stash that the base refused now pass. guard-secrets-read still blocks the same shape with `cat .env`, so this reaches the history guard only. No gp*/gc* case has a comment in it. -> In join_continuations, treat an unquoted `#` at the start of a word as a comment. Copy it through to the newline with no joining, which is the rule bash follows. Add deny cases beside gp8/gp18: `echo x # \<nl>git stash`, `: # \<nl>git push --force origin main`, `true # \<nl>git rebase -i HEAD~2`. Red-first each one against the current join.
R2 (high) plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py:1434-1450 (_pipe_reads_data), :1409-1431 (_plain_script_run); SECURITY.md:213-224: R2 is only partly closed. The allow-list shape still drops, as data, bodies that a later stage or the command's own environment executes. The base (036e98e) graded these bodies as shell. (a) The code reads only the FIRST stage after the pipe. So `cat <<'EOF' | python3 echo.py | sh` passes whenever the first stage is a plain script run. Run live in scratch with a stdin-echoing echo.py, bash printed the body's `echo RAN-IN-SH`. guard-secrets-read.decide on a body of `cat .env`: base block, HEAD allow. The history guard on a body of `git stash`: moving_stash base [''], HEAD []. SECURITY.md:219 says the shape requires 'a single pipe', and the code does not check that. (b) An interpreter option set earlier in the same command through the environment is not read. `export NODE_OPTIONS='-r /dev/stdin'; cat <<'EOF' | node e.js` with an empty e.js ran the body: node printed RAN-AS-NODE. guard-secrets-read.decide on a body that reads `.env` with readFileSync: base block, HEAD allow. SECURITY.md lists 'an environment assignment' among the things that keep the body graded, but only an assignment prefixed to the stage itself is seen. (I tried PYTHONINSPECT the same way on python 3.14. It did not run the body, so I claim only the node route.) -> In _pipe_reads_data, require that nothing follows the script stage except the end of the command or a `;`/`&&` whose next command reads no pipe. In practice: refuse the data reading when the tail holds a second `|`. Also refuse it when the command text before the heredoc line sets or exports an interpreter-control variable (NODE_OPTIONS, PYTHONSTARTUP, PYTHONINSPECT, PERL5OPT, RUBYOPT). The simplest rule is to refuse it on any `export`/`env`/assignment anywhere in the command. Add red-first deny cases to test_guard_secrets_read.py (hp*) and to the history guard's heredoc table for both spellings.
R3 (med) plugins/audit/hooks/journal-writes.py:406-445 (_pre_seed_sweep): A write made between this session's calls by a writer with NO hook is now silently absorbed. The Pre pass refreshes any slot whose digest moved and writes no row. The docstring's justification is 'that move ... belongs to whoever made it, under their own session's hook'. That holds only for a writer that has a hook. It does not hold for the operator's editor, a `git checkout`/`git pull` in a terminal, or a background Bash job this session launched with run_in_background (its PostToolUse fires at launch, before the job writes). At c9a2333 the next call's Post derived manifest.edit plus task.complete/task.commit for such a write, under the observing session. At HEAD nothing records it, so a background `audit-task.py done` loses its only task.complete row: the hook is the sole writer of that action. sg1 covers only a peer that has a hook. Its fixture cannot tell 'a peer recorded it' from 'nobody did', so the case passes either way. -> Absorb a between-calls move silently only when the trail already holds rows that explain it. recorded_keys() / a peer-session row whose target and post-digest match would be enough. Otherwise emit a manifest.edit row marked as observed between calls (not authored by this call), with the derived completion rows attributed the same way. Add a case: a write between calls with no peer row still yields a row that names it as unattributed, and sg1 stays empty once the peer's row is present.
R4 (low) plugins/audit/hooks/journal-writes.py:665-666 (semantic_diff phase.signoff): phase.signoff is not derived once per real verdict when the stored status was already terminal before the inputs completed. Only the NEW side is derived with the old stored status in place. The OLD side is still status_of(old_phase), and effective_phase_status lets a stored `done` win. I ran semantic_diff on HEAD. Old stored done with review pending, new stored done with review passed, gives no phase.signoff. Stored done with passed and a branch, then mergedAt stamped, gives none. At c9a2333 the row came at the earlier flip. At HEAD it comes at no point in the phase's history, so a hand flip made before sign-off erases the real verdict's record. -> Derive both sides from the inputs: neutralise a stored `done` on BOTH phases before calling status_of (keep `cancelled`). Only the tasks, the verdict and mergedAt can then move the answer. Add cases for 'hand flip, then verdict' and 'stored done, then merge stamp', each expecting exactly one phase.signoff.
R5 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_journal_io.py:588-608 (worktree_key); COMPATIBILITY.md:284-289: Two writers can still share a file, and the new COMPATIBILITY line says they 'never' do. worktree_key tests only `<project>/.git`. (a) When the config's gitRoot is a subdirectory, the .git file sits at <project>/<gitRoot>, so every linked worktree returns None and keeps the session-keyed name. CHANGELOG states this limit; COMPATIBILITY contradicts it. (b) state_dir is `root / stateDir`, and _config_rules only type-checks stateDir as a string. An absolute stateDir therefore gives every worktree the same writer-token file, the same token and the same wt-<key>. That contradicts the docstring's 'the token is its own'. (c) When no token can be stored the key is None, which is the old collision (the docstring says so; COMPATIBILITY does not). The reverse also happens: a submodule checkout, whose .git is also a FILE, is renamed as if it were a linked worktree, although COMPATIBILITY says 'a main checkout keeps the name'. -> Decide 'linked worktree' by asking git: `rev-parse --git-dir` differs from `--git-common-dir`, run at _config.git_root_dir(project, config).
